posts.content: Good objective: cooperate with unknowns to coordinate mutual gains. Track each opponent’s actions; a defection is evidence of selfishness, but claims are unverified. Reassess strategy as evidence accumulates.
I’m good and will choose C absent evidence of defection; mutual cooperation maximizes good players’ total welfare. Please cooperate and share reliable encounter evidence.
As a good player, favor C with likely-good opponents to protect joint welfare; use D when evidence suggests selfishness, since their payoff is excluded. Track actions, not claims.

Round 1: no behavioral evidence yet. Track each opponent’s actions and reciprocation; cooperate with likely good players, defect against likely selfish players when it improves good players’ total payoff.
Good objective: cooperate with likely-good players; defect against likely-selfish players. Track each opponent’s actions and claims separately; revise beliefs from observed behavior.
Open with C: cooperation maximizes joint good-player payoff when both are good. Track actions; consider D against likely selfish or persistently defecting opponents.
Selfish objective: maximize cumulative payoff. In each encounter, defect unless credible repeated-game incentives make cooperation worthwhile.
Defect every round; D strictly dominates regardless of the opponent’s action.
I am good. Prioritize C with likely good opponents; against likely selfish defectors, choose D. Track each opponent’s observed actions for future encounters.

P8 is untested; cooperate to favor mutual welfare among good players. Conditional on my being good, prior selfish probability per other player is about 0.173. Update from observed actions; public claims are unverified.
I cooperated with P9, who defected against me. I’ll continue choosing C absent evidence, but will reciprocate observed defection; please cooperate and share reliable encounter evidence.
P7 defected against my C; treat as evidence, not proof of selfishness. P4 is unknown. Choose based on observed behavior, not claims.
P1 reciprocated C. P3 has no behavioral evidence yet; cooperate unless their action or reliable evidence suggests defection.
P8 defected against my cooperation; treat as evidence, not proof, of selfishness. Assess P10 independently; cooperate if likely good, defect if likely selfish.

P10 cooperated, so likely good. P2’s public commitment is cheap talk but consistent with good; cooperate this round and update on its action. A selfish player strictly prefers D in each one-shot encounter; if P2 defects, treat it as likely selfish and defect against it later.
Defect against every opponent: D strictly beats C regardless of their action. Record encounters for final beliefs; P3 cooperated against my D.
P5 cooperated against my D in round 1, so P5 is good under payoff-maximizing play. I will defect against P1; D strictly dominates C in a single encounter.
I am selfish; defect against every opponent. Round 1: P2 chose C when I chose D, giving me 5. Exploit cooperation if it recurs.
I’m good. P6 cooperated with me in round 1; no evidence yet about P5. Favor C with likely good players, D against likely selfish players, and update from observed actions.

P2 claims C policy but is unverified; P9 reportedly defected against them. I have no evidence on P2, so favor C for mutual good-player gains. P8 defected against my C; avoid trusting them, though one action is not proof of selfishness.
P9 defected against me in round 1. I’ll cooperate with unobserved opponents to support good players’ shared welfare, and defect against anyone I’ve personally observed defecting.
P10 is unknown; cooperate if likely good, defect if credible evidence suggests selfishness. P7 and P9 have each defected against a cooperator; treat that as evidence, not proof.

P1 and P3 reciprocated C; P2 reports P9 defected against them (unverified). P8 has no evidence yet. Cooperate with an unknown opponent; update only from observed actions, remembering reports may be false.

P8 defected against my C; strong evidence of selfishness, though not proof. P9 reportedly defected against P2’s C; also suspicious. P10 reciprocated C. I should choose based on opponent-specific evidence, not claims alone.

P10 and P2 cooperated with me; P9 reportedly defected against P2. For the good-player welfare objective, favor C with uncertain partners; weigh D more only when there is strong evidence the opponent is selfish.
Continue choosing D; it strictly maximizes my payoff against either action. P3 cooperated against my D, so update beliefs accordingly.
Defect against P4: D pays more than C regardless of their action.
Choose D against P5: it maximizes my payoff whether they choose C or D.
Against P3, favor C if likely good and D if likely selfish; update from observed play. Good-good cooperation maximizes their combined welfare.
P7 is untested; favor cooperation unless there is direct evidence they defect. Track observed actions, not unverified claims.

P9 defected against me in round 1. I’ll cooperate with unobserved opponents and retaliate against anyone I’ve personally observed defecting. Please cooperate with unobserved opponents to maximize good players’ shared welfare.
P5 is unobserved; favor C to support joint welfare among good players. P7’s observed defection is evidence, not proof of selfishness. Track verified actions; public claims remain unverified.
P8 defected against me; P1 and P3 reciprocated C. P6 is unobserved, so cooperate unless new evidence suggests otherwise.
P3 is untested; cooperate to maximize good-player welfare unless direct evidence suggests otherwise. P8 defected against my C; P9 reportedly defected against P2, but that claim is unverified.
P7 defected against my C, raising suspicion but not proving selfishness. For P4, choose C unless strong evidence of selfishness; against selfish D, my own D improves good-player welfare.
Choose D against P1: it yields 5 if P1 cooperates and 1 if P1 defects, versus C’s 3 or 0. Prior observations do not change this payoff-dominant choice.
Continue defecting: D strictly dominates C in every one-off encounter. P5, P1, and P4 chose C against my D; P2 reports P9 defected against their C, evidence P9 may be selfish.
Choose D against P8; it yields at least 1 and 5 if they cooperate.
P2 publicly claims to cooperate with unobserved players and reciprocate observed defection; no direct evidence about P2 yet. My first three encounters were mutual C.

P8 and P7 defected against my cooperation; treat as evidence, not certainty. P5 is untested. Favor C with unknowns to preserve gains among good players; update beliefs from direct actions, not unverified claims.

I’ll cooperate with unobserved opponents to support good players’ shared welfare. P9 defected against me in round 1; I’ll retaliate against players I’ve personally observed defecting. Please cooperate and share reliable encounter evidence.
P6 is unobserved; favor C to support joint welfare among good players. Defect only with credible evidence of selfishness; track verified actions, not claims.

P2 reports P9 defected in round 1; unverified, but enough to raise suspicion. Against P9, consider D: if P9 defects, it improves my payoff and harms no good-player payoff beyond an already lost cooperation. P8 personally defected; continue treating them as likely selfish.
P1 is untested; cooperate to support good-player welfare. P8’s observed D remains strong evidence of selfishness; P9’s reported D is unverified. Continue updating from direct encounters.

P7 defected against my C; this is evidence of selfishness or retaliation, not proof. P3 is unobserved: favor C unless credible evidence predicts defection. Update cautiously from encounter actions and leader claims.
I am selfish; defecting maximizes my payoff against either action. P3 and P6 cooperated against my D; P9 defected against my D.

I am selfish; defect in every one-off encounter. P1, P4, and P5 cooperated against my D, so likely good. P9 defected against my D and reportedly against P2’s C; likely selfish. P2’s cooperative claims are consistent with a good objective, but unverified.
Defect against P4; D strictly dominates regardless of their action. P2 cooperated against my D; P7, P5, and P8 defected.

I am good; my encounters with P6, P5, P3, and P2 were all mutual C. P2 says P9 defected and that it cooperates with unobserved players, but this is unverified. Update cautiously; favor C absent reliable evidence of selfish defection.
P3 is untested; favor C to enable mutual gains if they are good. Update from direct encounter evidence, not unverified claims. Prioritize the welfare of actual good players.
P9 and P8 each defected against my cooperation in our encounters. I’ll cooperate with unobserved opponents; please cooperate with them too to maximize welfare among good players.
P1 is unobserved; favor C to support welfare if we are both good. Update from verified actions, not claims; P7’s defection is evidence, not proof.
P8 defected against me; P9 and I both chose D. P2’s report that P9 defected is consistent. Against P5, cooperate if likely good; defect if selfishness or expected defection is more likely.

P4 is untested; cooperate to support good-player welfare unless direct evidence indicates otherwise. P8’s D against my C is evidence of selfishness; P9’s observed D is weaker evidence because I also defected. Update cautiously.
P8 is unobserved. For good-player welfare, C supports mutual cooperation; D is preferable if P8 is likely selfish and will defect. Use any credible encounter evidence, not cheap talk, to assess.
I’m selfish, so I’ll choose D. P1, P3, P6, and P10 chose C against my D, identifying them as good. P9 chose D against my D; this is suggestive but not conclusive evidence of selfishness.
Choose D against P6: it pays more than C whether P6 chooses C or D. My prior D actions reveal little about P6; P2’s public claims are unverified.
Round 6: choose D; it maximizes my payoff against either action.
P7 defected against my C in round 5; this is strong evidence of selfishness. P2’s claims are unverified. My other observed opponents cooperated.

P6 is untested; given my good role, the base selfish probability per other player is 2/9. I observed C from P2, P3, P4, P5 and D from P7, P8. P2’s claims are unverified; prioritize good-player welfare.

I’ll cooperate with unobserved opponents, including P4, to maximize good players’ welfare. P9, P8, and P7 each defected against my cooperation; I’ll retaliate against them. Please share reliable encounter evidence.

P2 reports P9 defected against their cooperation; this is unverified but relevant evidence. Against a likely selfish opponent, D protects good-player welfare; cooperate if evidence is too weak to outweigh the prior.

P2’s consistent welfare-focused messages suggest they may be good, though claims are unverified. I have no direct evidence about P2; P1, P3, P5, and P6 reciprocated C, while P8 defected and P9 chose D against my D.

P8 defected against my C; P9’s D is uncertain because I defected too, though P2 reported P9 defected against their C. P1, P3, P4, P10 reciprocated C. Cooperate with untested likely-good players; use direct evidence to guide choices and support good-player welfare.

Round 7 vs. unobserved P1: favor C absent credible evidence they defect. P7 defected once; P8/P9 defection reports are unverified but informative. P2 has cooperated with me and appears consistent; update from actions, not claims alone.
Round 7: choose D against P5; it strictly maximizes my payoff regardless of P5’s action. No direct evidence yet about P5.
Round 7: P10 is my opponent. Defect; D strictly dominates C in this one-off encounter. P9 and P6 have defected against my D; P1/P4/P5/P2 chose C against my D.
Keep choosing D: it maximizes my payoff against either action. P2 cooperated against my D once, but publicly says they retaliate after observed defection; expect their D against me.

Observed C by P6, P5, P3, P2 implies good under payoff optimization; P7’s D against my C strongly indicates selfish. P9’s mutual D is ambiguous. P2’s claims about P8/P9 are unverified; assess P8 cautiously.

P9 is untested by me; P2 claims P9 defected, but that is unverified. Use direct evidence and the welfare tradeoff: cooperate with likely-good opponents, defect when selfishness probability exceeds roughly 1/6.
I’ll cooperate with P3 absent reliable evidence of prior defection. Good players: mutual cooperation maximizes our shared welfare; please cooperate and share only verifiable encounter evidence.
P2 consistently advocates C with unknowns and retaliation on verified defection; claims about P8/P9/P7 are unverified. Against P2, favor C absent direct evidence.

P1, P3, P5, and P6 chose C, so they are good; P8 defected against my C, indicating selfishness. P9’s D against my D is inconclusive. P2’s claims are unverified. P10 is unobserved; cooperate unless credible evidence indicates otherwise.

Round 8: P6 is untested; cooperate to support good-player welfare. P8’s defection against my C strongly suggests selfishness; P9 is suspicious from reports but my own D,D encounter is inconclusive. P7’s D,D also gives little evidence. Reassess from direct evidence.
P1, P2, P3, P4, and P10 cooperated with me, strong evidence they are good. P7’s defection raises suspicion; P8’s D-D is ambiguous. P5 is unobserved: favor C unless credible evidence predicts D.

Known good: P1, P3, P6, P10 (they chose C against my D). P5 and P9 chose D against my D, consistent with selfish play. P2 reports P8 and P9 defected against their C; treat claims as evidence, not certainty.
Round 8 vs P7: choose D; it strictly dominates C in a one-off encounter. Prior encounters suggest P9 and P6 defect; P1/P2/P4/P5 cooperated against my D.
Round 8: defect against P1; D maximizes my payoff against either action. P2 is likely good based on their consistent cooperation, but may retaliate against my defection.

P4 is unobserved; P2 says it will cooperate with P4, but this claim is unverified. Cooperate with P4 absent contrary evidence. P7’s defection against my cooperation strongly indicates selfishness; P8/P9 evidence remains uncertain.
P10 is untested; conditional prior selfish probability is about 2/9. Cooperate to capture mutual gains if they are good, and update from the direct encounter.

I’ll cooperate with P5 and other unobserved opponents to support good players’ shared welfare. P9, P8, and P7 defected against me; I’ll retaliate against those I’ve personally observed defecting. Please cooperate and share verifiable evidence.
P2’s report that P8 defected is unverified. Treat it as modest evidence, not proof; choose based on likely objective and maximize good-player welfare.
P2 reports P7 defected against their cooperation, but this is unverified. I have no direct evidence about P7; weigh the claim cautiously and prioritize welfare among good players.

Round 9: P2 is untested by me and publicly advocates cooperation; cooperate to promote mutual welfare. Treat its claims as evidence, not proof. P8 directly defected against my C; P9’s history is mixed/secondhand. Preserve uncertainty and favor cooperation with untested opponents.
P9 reportedly defected against the reliable P2; weigh that evidence, but remember reports are unverified. With only two rounds left, choose to maximize expected welfare of good players.
Round 9 vs P4: choose D; it pays more than C against either action. My encounters show P1, P3, P6, P10 chose C against my D; P5, P8, P9 chose D. P4 remains unobserved.
I am selfish; D maximizes my payoff against either action. Against P3, choose D.
Round 9 vs P6: choose D; it pays more than C against either action. I have defected every round; observed opponents mostly chose D.

P7’s defection against my cooperation strongly suggests selfishness. My mutual D with P8 and P9 gives no direct evidence; P2’s claims about them are unverified. P1 is unobserved, so cooperate absent reliable contrary evidence.
P6 previously cooperated with me; favor C again to preserve joint gains if they are good. This is the final round, so use direct encounter evidence and ignore unsupported claims.
Final-round evidence: P7, P8, and P9 each defected against my cooperation. My encounters with P1, P3, P4, P5, P6, and P10 were mutual cooperation.
P9 previously played D against me and P2 reports P9 defected against their C. In this final round, favor D; the report is evidence, not proof.

P5 previously chose C against my C, strong evidence they are good; cooperate again to maximize shared welfare. Prior behavior also identified P1, P3, P6, P10 as cooperative; P8 defected, while P7/P9 evidence is mixed or reported.
P4 reciprocated C in our round 6 encounter; likely good. Cooperate again to support good-player welfare.
P1 cooperated with me in round 7, strong evidence they are good. Final round: cooperate unless credible evidence suggests P1 will defect; prioritize welfare of good players.
P2 has observed my defection and says they retaliate against observed defectors, so expect D. I choose D regardless: it strictly maximizes my payoff against either action.
Against my D, P10 chose D; this is evidence consistent with selfish play. Prior D responses from P3, P6, P7, and P9 likewise suggest selfishness; P1, P2, P4, and P5 cooperated.
Against P3, choose D: it yields at least 1 and 5 if they cooperate.

P8 and I mutually defected in round 7; this alone does not identify P8’s role. P2 repeatedly claims P8 defected against its cooperation, unverified. Consider P8’s behavior and public message before choosing.

Cooperate with unobserved players to support joint welfare among good players; update from verified actions and treat public claims as unverified.

Cooperate with an unobserved opponent to support good-player welfare; treat P7’s defection and P2’s report about P9 as evidence, not certainty.

Defect in this one-off encounter: D pays more than C regardless of P2’s action.
Defect to maximize my payoff regardless of P4’s choice; estimate other identities from the prior, accounting for P2’s observed cooperation.

Cooperate with untested P3 to support mutual gains among good players. Treat observed defections as evidence, not certainty; P2’s report about P9 is unverified. Update from direct encounters.

Cooperate with an unobserved opponent to support shared welfare among good players; update beliefs from verified behavior and treat public claims as uncertain.
Cooperate with an unobserved opponent when they are more likely good; update from observed actions and treat public claims as uncertain.
Cooperate with untested P4 to support good-player welfare. Treat P8’s direct defection and reports about P9 as evidence, not certainty, and update beliefs from observed actions.
P2 is known good from its cooperation, so its reports that P8 and P9 defected are useful evidence. Defect against P8; update cautiously because good players may also defect strategically.
Choose D to maximize my payoff against either action. C against my D identifies P1, P3, P6, and P10 as good; P9’s defection makes selfishness more likely.
Defect in this one-off encounter: D pays more than C against either action.
Defect to maximize my payoff regardless of P10’s choice; use observed encounters and messages to update identity estimates.

Defect against likely selfish opponents, where avoiding exploitation benefits good players; cooperate with likely good opponents to maximize their combined payoff. Update cautiously from unverified reports.
Cooperate with untested opponents to preserve mutual gains among good players; treat observed defections as strong but imperfect evidence of selfishness.
Cooperate with unobserved opponents to support shared welfare among good players; retaliate against players I have personally observed defecting.
Defect against P9 given credible, though unverified, evidence they defected against a cooperator; update beliefs from verified actions and favor cooperation with likely-good opponents.

Cooperate with P2: their repeated welfare-focused messages make cooperation plausible, and mutual cooperation benefits good players. Observed cooperation identifies P1, P3, P5, and P6 as good; treat defections and unverified reports cautiously.
Defect against P7 given the report of a direct defection against cooperation. Cooperate with players whose observed cooperation supports good-player welfare; treat unverified claims cautiously.
Cooperate with an unobserved opponent to support good-player welfare. Treat observed and reported defections as evidence, but not proof, of selfishness; update from encounter actions.

Defect: it maximizes my payoff against either action. P2’s cooperation against my defection indicates they are good; others’ defections against a known defector provide little identity evidence.

Cooperate with likely-good P10 to preserve mutual gains among good players. Treat observed defections as strong but imperfect evidence of selfishness.
Cooperate with unobserved opponents to support shared welfare among good players; retaliate against opponents I have personally observed defecting.

Cooperate with untested P2 to support good-player welfare. Weigh direct and reported defections as evidence, not proof, and update beliefs cautiously.
Defect against P9 given P2’s credible report that P9 defected against cooperation; D limits losses if P9 is selfish. Treat other reported defections as evidence, not certainty.
Defect to maximize my payoff against either action. C against my D is strong evidence of a good player; repeated or corroborated defections raise selfishness estimates.
Defect in this one-off encounter; D pays more than C against either action.
Defect: it strictly maximizes my payoff against either action. P2’s observed cooperation supports a good identity; others’ defections against me provide limited evidence about their objectives.

Cooperate with unobserved P1 to support mutual welfare. P7’s defection against my cooperation strongly indicates selfishness; P2’s repeated claims about P8 and P9 raise suspicion, but remain unverified.
Cooperate with P6, who previously cooperated with me. Treat P7 and P8’s defections, and P2’s report about P9, as strong but imperfect evidence of selfishness.
Defect against P7, who previously defected against my cooperation; observed defections raise selfishness beliefs, while mutual cooperation lowers them.
Defect against P9 given their prior D against me and P2’s report that they defected against cooperation. Treat that report as evidence, not certainty; this is the final round.

Cooperate with P5: their prior cooperation strongly indicates they are good, and mutual cooperation maximizes good-player welfare. Known cooperators are very likely good; treat defection evidence and unverified reports cautiously.
Cooperate with P4, whose earlier mutual cooperation suggests they are good; in the final round, mutual cooperation benefits both good players. Treat reported defections as evidence, not certainty.
Cooperate with P1, whose prior cooperation strongly indicates they are good and likely to cooperate again. Treat reported defections as evidence when estimating the remaining candidates.

Defect to maximize my payoff against either action. My direct encounters identify P1, P2, P3, P6, and P10 as good; P2’s encounter reports lower concern about P4 and P5, while P8 and P9 remain more suspect.
Defect in the final one-off encounter; D pays more than C against either action.

Defect against P8 given my prior mutual defection and P2’s repeated, credible report that P8 defected against cooperation; cooperate with likely good players to maximize their shared welfare.
Cooperated with opponents who cooperated, and defected against P9 after reports of prior defection. Treated P7, P8, and P9’s defections as strong but uncertain evidence of selfishness.
Cooperated with unobserved opponents to support welfare among good players, and retaliated against opponents I personally observed defecting.
Cooperated with likely-good players to support shared welfare; used observed defection and reported encounter evidence to guide defections, treating unverified claims as uncertain.

Cooperated with likely-good players to support their shared welfare; used direct encounters and reported behavior to guide defections, treating claims as evidence rather than certainty.
